1. **F1 [high] REQ-2 is not satisfied because `jit apply` locks `apply.lock`, but normal issue/dependency writers do not participate in that lock.** `apply_template_with` acquires `APPLY_LOCK` at [crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:231), and `repo_write_lock` locks the caller-provided filename at [crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:1054). However `JsonFileStorage::save_issue`, `delete_issue`, and `list_issues` use `.index.lock` and per-issue locks, not `apply.lock`, at [crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:503), [crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:644), and [crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:671). A concurrent `jit issue create`, `jit dep add`, or other writer can therefore mutate the store after the pre-apply snapshot and during commit. On failure, rollback treats every issue absent from the pre-apply snapshot as apply-created and deletes it, and reverts changed pre-existing issues at [crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:549). This can erase unrelated concurrent work and means the apply is not actually atomic with respect to repository mutations.
